units.title: 1. Definition, Classification Subtypes and AIDP Pathophysiology
units.guide:
GBS is acute (<=4 weeks) bilaterally symmetrical inflammatory autoimmune polyradiculoneuropathy; CIDP is its chronic (>8 weeks) counterpart.
Subtypes: AIDP (anti-GM1, demyelinating, best prognosis), AMAN (children and young adults, anti-GD1a, axonal), AMSAN (mostly adults, axonal) and MFS (rarest; ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, areflexia; anti-GQ1b); AMAN, AMSAN and MFS share poor prognosis and all antibodies are IgGs.
AIDP is m/c with mean age 40 years and male > female; antibodies bind myelin, activate complement, invite macrophage invasion and cause vesicular degeneration.

units.title: 2. Clinical Presentation, Examination, Progression and Prognosis
units.guide:
Presentation flows from sensory symptoms (B/L tingling and numbness of lower limbs, rubbery legs) through mild transient bowel and bladder dysfunction to motor symptoms (bilateral lower limb weakness).
Examination early shows normal higher mental function, cranial nerves and upper limb motor with bilateral atonic areflexic paraparesis (proximal + distal) of lower limbs and large fibre (A-alpha) sensory loss.
Progression is rapid: >=24 hours since incident, areflexic ascending paralysis from lower to upper limb, cranial nerve involvement in 30% (4-15% mortality), brainstem involvement, respiratory centre affection and ventilation. 80% recover (5-10% with persistent weakness); survival is 85-90% with early intervention; bad prognostic factors are ANS manifestations.

units.title: 3. Inciting Factors and Diagnostic Criteria
units.guide:
Inciting factors: gastroenteritis/URTI in the past 4 weeks in 60-70% of GBS cases; associated infections C. jejuni, CMV, EBV, mycoplasma, Hep A/B and HIV; vaccination association; molecular mimicry. C. jejuni also links to IPSID.
Essential features are progressive weakness in both arms and legs (legs -> arms) and areflexia; strong support includes progression over days up to 4 weeks, relative symmetry, mild sensory signs, cranial nerve involvement (m/c VII > III, B/L LMN VII palsy with sarcoidosis as D/d), recovery beginning 2-4 weeks after progression ceases, autonomic dysfunction and absence of fever at onset.
Lumbar puncture shows albuminocytological dissociation in 90% (not detected <7 days and in GBS variants), pleocytosis of 10-30 cells in 5%, findings lasting only 1 month; NCS shows latency prolongation, conduction block, reduced velocity, absent or prolonged F-wave and H reflex and temporal dispersion. Exclusions: botulism, myasthenia gravis, diphtheria, abnormal porphyrin metabolism and pure sensory syndrome.

units.title: 4. Treatment, MFS/Bickerstaff Encephalitis and CIDP vs AIDP
units.sec: GBS Treatment, MFS/Bickerstaff & CIDP vs AIDP
units.guide:
Treatment: IVIg 0.4 gm/kg x 5 days; PLEX (one filter : 5 cycles) preferred for ANS manifestations, each cycle removing 1.5 times plasma volume replaced with 50% NS and 50% FFP; no role for steroids.
MFS (ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, areflexia, anti-GQ1b +) plus brain stem encephalitis and hyperreflexia defines Bickerstaff encephalitis; treatment is PLEX.
CIDP runs >8 weeks with subacute/chronic non-emergency presentation, 30% preceding infection, secondary causes (myeloma/POEMS/HIV/SLE/Hodgkins/DM/IBD), absent ANS symptoms, 10% cranial nerve involvement, no precise onset point, no ventilator need and nil mortality; treatment is steroid (DOC), PLEX for resistant cases and IVIg for pure motor CIDP, whereas AIDP uses IVIg/PLEX and not steroids.

units.title: 5. CIDP Affected Systems, POEMS Syndrome and MMN-CB
units.guide:
CIDP shows prominent sensory involvement with large fibre symptoms and distal-to-proximal spread plus gradually progressive distal-to-proximal lower-limb-predominant motor symptoms, while AIDP is predominantly motor with minimal sensory involvement.
CIDP is associated with relapsing neuropathy and nerve thickening; large fibre sensory symptoms are tingling, numbness, dysesthesia, paraesthesia, cotton wool sensation and sensory ataxia; nerve thickening also occurs in leprosy and CMT.
POEMS shows increased VEGF, lambda light chain myeloma, polyneuropathy referring to CIDP and osteosclerotic lesions, with Castleman syndrome refractory to therapy. MMN-CB is a pure motor neuropathy with atrophy lasting years, asymmetric, upper limb predominant, demyelinating on NCS with anti-GM1 antibody (D/d GBS); other pure motor causes are lead poisoning and dapsone toxicity.
